title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment that tested whether inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration/execution deviations materially constrain inference: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per-condition generation; and (2) a prespecified comparison (GVR vs a schema-constrained baseline, C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no additional verifier-detectable benefit under the executed semantics, model, task bank, and verifier. We release and analyze the archived artifacts and recommend reproducible follow-ups (independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model runs, and expanded verifier coverage).

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiency but raises substantive safety concerns: stochastic generators can emit syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, workflow ordering, or security predicates). Research and practitioner guidance therefore commonly recommend interposing deterministic validators and iterative repair—generate–verify–repair (GVR)—so that mechanically checkable defects are detected and corrected before execution. Despite that recommendation, rigorous confirmatory evidence quantifying GVR’s verifier-detectable benefit under preregistered, paired designs is limited.

We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) to answer a focused operational question: does a bounded GVR intervention reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to (A) unconstrained LLM generation and (B) schema-constrained decoding on a public synthetic NetOps task bank when measured in a paired design? The preregistered estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, and the analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 was frozen before data collection (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d). Our contributions are (1) a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic pybatfish-style verifier; (2) transparent execution accounting that documents shared-initial-candidate semantics and complete episode accounting; (3) confirmatory statistics showing a degenerate null outcome (zero discordant pairs) together with an explicit reconciliation of preregistered power assumptions and executed semantics; and (4) reproducible, operational recommendations for evaluation designs that can legitimately test GVR’s value under generator stochasticity.
sections.related_work:
Three strands of prior work motivated the study. First, cross-domain surveys and empirical reports document that LLMs can hallucinate and produce fabricated or incorrect code-like outputs, motivating verifier-interposed pipelines to reduce operational risk [10.1145/3728894,10.36227/techrxiv.177219979.94060974/v1]. Second, generate–verify–repair and constrained-decoding methods have been shown to increase syntactic and executable correctness (compilation, grammar validity) and to reduce surface-level hallucinations; case studies report practical gains for mechanically checkable properties but leave open semantic correctness for domain-specific invariants [10.2139/ssrn.6754899,10.26434/chemrxiv.15005091/v1]. Third, NetOps-specific research emphasizes verifier-driven evaluation (reachability and policy invariants), intent-based translation prototypes, and governance patterns that combine automated checks with human oversight for high-stakes changes [10.1145/3656296,10.1145/3718958.3750537].

Two methodological gaps identified in that literature informed our preregistered design: (G1) a scarcity of standardized benchmarks measuring semantic and operational correctness (policy conformance, reachability) rather than only surface syntax, and (G2) limited empirical evidence integrating stochastic LLM generation with formal or stronger symbolic verification at scale. Our study targeted GVR’s operational effect on verifier-encoded invariants within a reproducible paired framework to address these gaps experimentally.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand: The study was preregistered (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1; preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d). The primary estimand is the paired difference in verifier-detected semantic-violation rates (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Two primary comparisons were prespecified: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding; Bonferroni correction across those two comparisons was recorded (family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). The analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' and the sampling plan (N=240 paired tasks) were frozen prior to execution.

Execution contract and key frozen semantics: The adapter family executing the run is archived as hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the requested generator was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The deterministic verifier used for scoring and structured diagnostics was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Crucially, the preregistration-recorded generation_semantics executed in the run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1), meaning a single generator output per task was produced and reused across the arms. The repair policy allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1) and maximum_model_calls budget = 480.

Task bank and oracle: The public synthetic NetOps task bank (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks = 240 tasks) encodes initial states, intents, required workflow constraints, and expected final states. The deterministic validator returns structured diagnostics (violation_count, violations list, parsed_command_count, required_command_count); scoring used the 'full_intent_constraint_validation' rule in validator_version 5.0. Representative task manifests and validator traces are archived and authoritative for reported difficulty levels and per-task scoring decisions.

Planned analysis: The preregistered primary test was a paired McNemar-style exact test implemented by the frozen executor, with absolute risk reduction and 95% Wilson CIs reported. A paired-bootstrap percentile CI was also prespecified and used (bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness and exclusion rules were preregistered: irrecoverable infra/model-call failures were to be handled per the executor's 'complete_pair_primary' rules and recorded in the execution manifest.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed): The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 240, and model_calls_used = 240 (shared-initial-candidate semantics produced a single generation per task reused for both scored conditions). Representative scoring JSON files and response artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json and execution/responses/*.txt) show that for every task the shared initial candidate was identical to both arm responses and that validator validation_before and validation_after blocks report violation_count = 0.

Primary confirmatory outcomes: The preregistered paired analysis produced contingency counts n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Observed rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) are archived and authoritative for these numbers.

Repair loop diagnostics: The validator traces record repair_applied = false for every episode; the bounded repair loop never executed because the shared initial candidate satisfied validator predicates in all tasks. Contamination and missingness summaries are empty and record zero failures.

Statistical interpretation and degeneracy: With zero discordant within-pair outcomes (n10 = n01 = 0), the paired McNemar test is degenerate—no within-pair information exists to estimate a differential effect. The observed exact p-value p = 1.00 and the collapsed bootstrap CI are deterministic consequences of the contingency table under the prespecified analysis executor. Importantly, this degeneracy is a direct consequence of two artifact-backed facts: (a) the generator+prompt pairing produced verifier-acceptable outputs for every task, and (b) the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics removed independent per-arm stochastic variation that could have produced discordance. The preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation; because that assumption did not hold in the executed semantics, the preregistered power argument does not apply to the observed data.
sections.discussion:
Conservative interpretation: Under the executed, artifact-backed conditions—single generator pairing (gpt-5-mini), deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), synthetic task bank (N = 240), one shared generation per task reused across arms, and a bounded single-repair budget—bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. This is a narrowly scoped, artifact-grounded empirical statement and does not imply general ineffectiveness of GVR for other generators, independent-generation semantics, adversarial inputs, extended repair budgets, or richer verifiers.

Two preregistration→execution deviations that affect inference (archival evidence): (i) generation semantics mismatch: the preregistered power calculation and inferential logic assumed independent per-condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true) but the archived execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) and therefore deterministically reduced discordance potential and invalidated the original power assumption; (ii) unexecuted prespecified comparison: the preregistration listed two prespecified primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B). The archived run executed only the adapter-configured paired experiment comparing unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared_initial_candidate semantics; the prespecified schema-constrained baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale for its omission appears in the execution artifacts. Both deviations are disclosed and documented in the archived manifests.

Practical implications for evaluation design: Demonstrating GVR’s verifier-detectable value requires evaluation semantics and inputs that permit within-pair discordance and verifier sensitivity. We recommend (artifact-grounded): (1) re-executing the preregistered design with independent per-condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true) to restore discordance potential using the archived task manifest and RNG seeds; (2) injecting adversarial or golden-reference tasks (the preregistration planned 10% golden tasks) whose expected verifier outcome is known to validate oracle sensitivity; (3) expanding the generator set beyond gpt-5-mini to test cross-model generality; (4) increasing allowed repair iterations and recording iteration distributions to assess diminishing returns or overfitting to the verifier; and (5) broadening verifier coverage (additional semantic invariants or formal/SMT hybrids) to reduce oracle incompleteness risk. These recommendations follow directly from the execution artifacts and from gaps identified in the evidence synthesis (G1–G3).

Threats to validity: Internal validity—affected by the preregistration/power mismatch (shared-generation vs independent-generation) and by the bounded repair budget; Construct validity—passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 does not guarantee absence of operational risks outside the verifier’s encoded invariants; External validity—results derive from a synthetic task bank, a single model (gpt-5-mini), a single bounded repair budget, and one verifier; Conclusion validity—zero discordant pairs prevent evidence for GVR efficacy under the executed semantics. All of these threats are recorded in the archived manifest and analysis artifacts and are summarized in the limitations below.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics (one shared generation per task reused across arms), every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a null paired estimate (0.0), exact McNemar p = 1.00, and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR did not add verifier-detectable value in this specific artifact-grounded setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. However, two preregistration/execution deviations materially constrain inference: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption; and (2) a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no rationale is recorded in the archive. We therefore do not generalize beyond the specific model, prompt, task bank, verifier, repair budget, or generation semantics. We publish the authoritative archived artifacts so others can reproduce the accounting and re-run alternative independent-generation, adversarial, and multi-model regimes to more robustly assess GVR’s operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
